clue.text: One chap about to be caught by the law gets to flee, being scared

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within it, so the law closes round the rest

parts.note: the law can be called the rule

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the one-and-chap pair is read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow about to be arrested decides to make a run for it in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the one-and-chap pair to give NAMI. 'gets to' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for running away from something out of fear or reluctance is to bolt a great distance.

clue.text: Second charge makes man on field poorly

parts.note: the referee, ref, is the official on the football field
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A referee falls ill and gets charged a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a second filling or charge, as of a glass or a pen.

clue.text: Girl has two lines at right angles — either may be so designated

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name
the letter L is formed of two strokes at right angles

explanation.surface: A girl draws two perpendicular lines in geometry class.
explanation.walkthrough: In geometry a line perpendicular to another is called its normal, so either of the two lines can be given that name.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a perpendicular is called a normal, so each of the two lines meeting at right angles is one.

clue.text: Males catching a reptile with enormous great structure

indicators.note: catching means the males enclose what follows

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two males give MM
croc is short for crocodile, a reptile
OS stands for outsize, enormous

explanation.surface: Men grab a crocodile with an enormous construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A macrocosm is the whole great structure of the universe, as against the small world of man.

clue.text: Bringer of clear sight, I? I'm dicey — deadly, possibly

definitions.text: Bringer of clear sight, I? I'm dicey — deadly, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A drug speaks, claiming to give clear vision while admitting it is risky and maybe lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: All of 'clear sight, I? I'm dicey — deadly' is anagram fodder for the full name of LSD, and the whole clue is its own description.
explanation.definitionFit: LSD is a hallucinogen claimed by users to sharpen perception, yet it is a risky and potentially dangerous drug.

clue.text: Idiot's kept by phone — one left hanging?

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so the phone surrounds the idiot

parts.note: TEL is the standard abbreviation for telephone
an idiot is an ass; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A fool is stuck on the phone, left dangling at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a decorative tuft that dangles from a cushion, curtain or cap, so it is cryptically something left to hang.

clue.text: Is "embracing silver time"? On the contrary!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Is "embracing silver time"? On the contrary!', has wordplay only (AG + T around IS) and no word that defines AGIST (to graze livestock for payment); the definition appears to be missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Is "embracing silver time"? On the contrary!

clue.text: Look for floating structure in the sound — any sort of ship

indicators.note: in the sound means as heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: to look for is to seek, and a floating structure is a raft

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a raft adrift in a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a sea channel, fitting the maritime picture, but it signals hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Seacraft are vessels of any kind used at sea.

clue.text: They suck blood from fish, light fish, audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a lamp is a light and rays are flat fish

explanation.surface: Bloodsuckers attack fish that glow.
explanation.definitionFit: These eel-like jawless fish attach to other fish and feed on their blood.

clue.text: Divine citadel giving city a second protection

indicators.note: the citadel gives protection by surrounding the other pieces, as walls would

parts.note: a citadel is a fort
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A fortress lends a town its walls for a moment's safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb here, to foretell, not an adjective about the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict what will happen, which is what a prediction of the weather or results does.

clue.text: Train off line? Mangle is seen inside

indicators.note: the word is is seen placed inside the mangling word

parts.note: to mangle is to maim

explanation.surface: A railway train comes off the track and a wreck is visible within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a verb here: to train a gun off the line of the target is to aim badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a weapon off target is to point it wrongly, a fresh disguise for a bad shot.

clue.text: See 4
Plain Welsh town that must have faulty name dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the faulty name is taken away from the town

parts.note: Llandudno is a seaside resort town in north Wales
something faulty is a dud

explanation.surface: A plain little Welsh town has to lose its badly chosen name.
explanation.walkthrough: LLANDUDNO, a resort in north Wales, loses DUDN to leave the Spanish-American word for a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy treeless plain of the kind found in northern South America.

clue.text: One can disturb retirer so!

indicators.note: to disturb is to throw into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy reveller is the sort who wakes up a person who has gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous merrymaker is exactly someone whose racket would wake a sleeper, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Golly, almost by implication, split costs evenly!

parts.note: Golly cut short leaves GO followed by two Ls, and each L is the Roman numeral for fifty, implied rather than written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise before agreeing to share the bill equally.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the Y of 'Golly' ('almost') leaves GO + L + L; 'by implication' asks you to read each Roman L as fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to share something equally, half each, as with a bill.

clue.text: Spooner's desire — game at Eton with loud-mouthed women

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping word beginnings, signals the swap

parts.note: a desire is a wish
Eton fives is a handball game played in a court at Eton College

explanation.surface: A Spooner type longs for a schoolboy ball game played amid shouting women.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of WISH and FIVES gives FISH WIVES. Fives is a British handball game played against walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishwives, once market sellers of fish, are by extension coarse, shrill-voiced women.

clue.text: Old England batsman with hit coming from the meat

parts.note: Allan Lamb was an England Test batsman of the 1980s and 90s
a chop is a cutting blow or hit

explanation.surface: A former England batsman makes a stroke off the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chop is a downward cutting shot, fitting the batsman picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a cut of meat from a young sheep.

clue.text: Audibly loses control suddenly when drunk? It's the strong booze

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: someone who loses control suddenly snaps

explanation.surface: A drinker is heard flying into a rage after too much strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' tells you to slur the word: said by a drunk, the S comes out as SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled spirit, a type of hard liquor.

clue.text: In America my act's possibly associated with piano and contralto

definitions.text: In America my act's possibly associated with piano and contralto

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A performer in the States says their act always involves a piano and a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling with a Y is the American variant, hence 'In America'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accompanist plays the piano beside a singer such as a contralto, and this spelling is the US form.

clue.text: Cliff hard to miss — on top there's superb stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top places the superb word before the rest

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means superb

indicators.note: to miss means the hard part is left out of the name

parts.note: Cliff Richard is the British pop singer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer must skip hard tasks while someone above praises the material.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop star; RICHARD without HARD leaves RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or material, so it is stuff in the sense of textile.

clue.text: Overseas character Haynes? Famous cricketer of yesteryear

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from overseas
Desmond Haynes, the West Indies opener, may be called Des

explanation.surface: A West Indian cricketer is recalled as a great player of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilfred Rhodes was an England all-rounder who played Test cricket until he was 52.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Rhodes was a celebrated Yorkshire and England cricketer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: With head back, beast has knocked out daughter — it's in danger from a bull!

definitions.text: it's in danger from a bull!

indicators.note: back means the word for head is read in reverse

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: knocked out means the daughter is removed from the beast

parts.note: an echidna is a spiny anteater, an Australian beast

explanation.surface: An animal throws its head back after knocking a girl flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With head back' gives BON; ECHIDNA, the spiny anteater, minus D gives ECHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain is the proverbial victim of a bull in a china shop, a playful way to define it.

clue.text: Rail about dissolute man making progress?

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A railing about a debauched man's advance, echoing Hogarth's rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a fence or railway; it is a marsh bird. 'making progress?' nods to Hogarth's A Rake's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The crake is a bird of the rail family, such as the corncrake.

clue.text: Scot's extreme but pointless position brings violent indignation

indicators.note: pointless means losing the point, here the headland word cape

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the extreme north-west tip of mainland Scotland

explanation.surface: An outlying Scottish spot that seems useless provokes furious anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is the north-western extremity of Scotland; a cape is a point of land, so 'pointless' drops CAPE. 'position' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is fierce anger, a synonym for violent indignation.

clue.text: Group leader seen outside gym

indicators.note: the leader is seen on the outside, surrounding the gym

parts.note: a head is a leader
PT, physical training, is gym class

explanation.surface: A group's leader is spotted outside the gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a set of seven, so it names a particular group.

clue.text: Doing the rounds, delivers the Mirror — must be this?

indicators.note: doing the rounds suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paperboy on his round delivers the Mirror newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Mirror' looks like the newspaper; it is a looking-glass, which must be coated with silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass mirror is backed with a thin metallic coating, so it must be coated that way.

clue.text: More luxurious model astride horse

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the model goes round the horse

parts.note: one who models or poses is a poser
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A fashion model sits astride a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means smart and luxurious, so the comparative form means more luxurious.

clue.text: England footballer incorporates special decoration in night attire

indicators.note: incorporates means takes inside, so the footballer holds the decoration

parts.note: Becks is the nickname of England footballer David Beckham
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military decoration

explanation.surface: An England football star receives a medal and is pictured in his nightwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed socks are warm socks worn in bed, part of what one wears at night.
